title: Date Parser
story: Your app receives dates from a form in 'DD/MM/YYYY' format, but users sometimes type garbage like '99/99/9999' or 'hello/there/world'. Instead of crashing, you need to parse safely and return either a valid date tuple or a clear error.
why: Parsing structured text into typed data with Result is the foundation of every data pipeline.
analogy: Parsing a date string is like opening a letter with three compartments. First you check the envelope is the right size (length 10), then verify the dividers are in the right places (slashes at position 2 and 5), then read each compartment's number — if any compartment has scribbles instead of digits, you return the letter unread.
try_it: Parse these dates and observe the errors: '01/01/2025' (valid), '1/1/2025' (too short), '01-01-2025' (wrong separators), '99/99/2025' (out of range). Add a check for month-specific day limits (e.g., February max 29, April max 30).
tips: `string.str_slice(s, start, end)` takes inclusive start and exclusive end — slice(2, 3) gives character at index 2
The `?` operator on `string.str_to_int` automatically returns `Err` if parsing fails — no manual match needed
Destructure tuples in `match` with `Ok((d, m, y)) =>` to extract all three values at once
common_mistakes: Forgetting to check the slashes — '01-01-2025' would parse as valid numbers but the format is wrong
Using `string.str_to_int()` without `?` — the function returns `Result[Int, Str]`, not a plain `Int`
